gaps.explanation: Plural general nouns and flu (illness name) take no article.

gaps.sentence: The novel had a huge effect on ___ young people of the 1960s.
gaps.explanation: 'The young people of the 1960s' — defined by the of-phrase, so 'the'.
'MA' is pronounced /em/, starting with a vowel sound, so 'an MA'.

gaps.sentence: She put ___ money in the safe before leaving.
gaps.explanation: 'The money' and 'the safe' are specific in the situation.

gaps.sentence: ___ bicycles are a cheap way of seeing the city.
gaps.explanation: Plural nouns in a general sense take no article.

gaps.sentence: The tour included ___ visit to the British Museum.
gaps.explanation: 'A visit' (one of many possible) and 'the British Museum' (museums take 'the').

gaps.sentence: She spent three weeks in ___ hospital after the accident.
gaps.explanation: British English: be in hospital (as a patient) takes no article; the building is the hospital.

gaps.sentence: Could you pass me ___ salt, please?
gaps.explanation: 'The salt' — both speakers know which one (on the table).
